title: Invariant basis number for nontrivial commutative rings
statement: Let $R$ be a nontrivial commutative ring. Then $R$ has invariant basis number: for natural numbers $m,n$, every $R$-linear equivalence $(\operatorname{Fin} m\to R)\simeq_R(\operatorname{Fin} n\to R)$ implies $m=n$.

source.place: Elementary invariant-rank argument accompanying Example 3.1; general commutative-ring fact implemented by Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/InvariantBasisNumber.lean:313–317.

proof.text: Apply the exact Mathlib instance invariantBasisNumber_of_nontrivial_of_commRing. Its proof chooses a maximal ideal I of R, transports the supplied finite free equivalence to the residue field R/I using inducedEquiv and Ideal.piQuotEquiv, then applies eq_of_fin_equiv over that field. Thus the finite ranks agree, including rank zero.
